# Tessera

> Tessera is a programming language for software that language models write and people review. It has a small, regular syntax; a function declares what it can do with `uses` and is pure without it; a `note` keeps the reason for a decision next to the code; and programs compile to safe Rust. Its design decisions are made by measurement, not by taste: a harness has models solve tasks from the reference alone, compiles every answer, and records pass rate and token cost per variant of the language.

Tessera is an early proof of concept under the MIT licence. The syntax and the compiler are not stable, and Tessera must not be relied on as a security guarantee.

To write Tessera, read the language reference below first. It is the whole language in one file, and it is what the harness gives a model.

## Docs

- [Language reference](https://tessera-language.com/llms-full.txt): the complete language in one file: types, effects, syntax, the standard library, the diagnostics and the runtime errors.
- [Why Tessera](https://tessera-language.com/why): the argument for a language aimed at models that people still review.
- [The language](https://tessera-language.com/language): a guided tour with examples.
- [How it works](https://tessera-language.com/how): the compilers, the runtime and the measurement harness.
- [Get Tessera](https://tessera-language.com/get): building the toolchain and compiling a first program.

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/dib0/Tessera-language): specification, both compilers, runtime, standard modules, harness and examples.
- [Specification](https://github.com/dib0/Tessera-language/blob/main/language-design.md): the authoritative description of the language. Where the compiler and the specification disagree, the specification wins.
- [Examples](https://github.com/dib0/Tessera-language/tree/main/examples): complete programs, from a few lines to a game.
- [Standard modules](https://github.com/dib0/Tessera-language/tree/main/std): the modules that ship with the compiler, written in Tessera.

## Optional

- [Measurement harness](https://github.com/dib0/Tessera-language/tree/main/harness): the tasks, the variants and the method behind the design decisions.
- [Tesseradoom](https://github.com/dib0/Tessera-language/tree/main/examples/tesseradoom): a DOOM-style engine in Tessera, the largest example and the test bed for new features.
- [Web hosts](https://github.com/dib0/Tessera-language/blob/main/hosts/README.md): running a Tessera web application as CGI, FastCGI, a server, or a module inside nginx, Apache or IIS.
